title: KV pager coalescer and eviction-policy refactor to reduce fragmentation and scheduler stalls
author: Evan Park
description: Motivation: We observed increased KV-cache fragmentation under mixed-length sequence workloads and continuous batching at high QPS; fragmentation combined with on-demand spillover was producing long reclamation stalls that amplified scheduler tails. This PR introduces a coordinated pager coalescer and a refactor of eviction selection/reclamation to reduce fragmentation, smooth spillover behavior, and make eviction decisions scheduler-aware. Summary of changes: 1) Pager coalescer: a background coalescer merges small adjacent free page segments within a region when fragmentation score > region_compact_threshold; compaction is windowed and rate-limited to avoid interfering with latency SLOs. 2) Fragmentation scoring: per-region moving-score (hotness-weighted) that factors in recent allocation/deallocation patterns and KV access counts; regions with low hotness but high fragmentation are prioritized for coalescing. 3) Eviction refactor: split the old monolithic evictor into selector + reclaim worker. Selector ranks candidates using a hybrid score (access_freq, prefix_affinity, fragment_penalty, estimated_reclaim_cost). Reclaim worker performs the memory ops and integrates with the pager coalescer to opportunistically coalesce freed space. 4) Spill controller: when memory pressure crosses spill_threshold, spill controller ramps controlled background spill tasks to disk with a token bucket rate limiter to prevent bursty I/O from stalling the scheduler. 5) Scheduler hooks: batching_scheduler now annotates batch edges and informs the selector about latency-critical batches; selector preserves hot prefixes for in-flight continuous batches to avoid KV cache churn on tail requests. 6) Allocator improvements: alignment-aware allocations to reduce internal fragmentation for commonly-seen small KV entries; lightweight freelist per-alignment class to speed small allocs. 7) Observability: new metrics (kv.region_fragmentation, kv.coalesce_ops{duration}, kv.eviction_reclaim_latency, kv.spill_rate) and tracing points added to trace_tools. Benchmarks & results: microbench on pager_bench.py with mixed short/long sequence traffic (60/40) at 20k qps shows: - 9-12% p95 latency improvement for generation paths that hit KV cache - 18% reduction in long-tail reclamation pauses (measured by kv.eviction_reclaim_latency p99) - steady-state memory footprint reduced by ~7% on workloads with small-churn prefixes Continuous-batching integration: experiments show the selector's prefix-affinity scoring prevents unnecessary eviction of in-flight prefixes and reduces rewarm misses by ~35% under bursty traffic. CI & tests: added unit coverage for pager coalescer and eviction selector (tests/kv/*). First CI run exposed a flaky integration test (test_eviction_integration) due to scheduling races; added deterministic waits and trace assertions and re-ran. All CI checks green on final run. Backwards compatibility & config knobs: preserved all existing config defaults; new runtime knobs added under kv.coalescer.{enabled,window_ms,rate_limit}, kv.evictor.{spill_threshold,selector_decay_ms} and documented in docs/ops/kv-tuning.md. Migration and rollout: non-breaking, can be toggled off via kv.coalescer.enabled. Suggested gradual rollout: enable in staging for 48h with hourly kv.* metrics, then canary 5-10% traffic, then full rollout. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-9843) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Benchmarks attached - [x] Docs updated - [x] Feature flag and config knobs - [x] Observability added Commits: - 8c3f2b4 add pager coalescer skeleton and config - f24b9a1 implement fragmentation scoring and tests - a3d5e21 split evictor into selector + reclaim worker - 1fc4d7b allocator alignment optimizations - 5b0e9da scheduler hooks and prefix-affinity scoring - c12fef8 add spill controller and rate limiter - 9d71b3c benchmarks, docs, and CI test fixes Review thread summary: Lena Cho requested clearer metrics and an explicit knob to disable coalescing during maintenance windows; implemented kv.coalescer.enabled and added documentation. Marcus Liu asked for microbench numbers and an end-to-end trace example; attached pager_bench.py results and a perf trace under tools/trace_tools. Priya Nambiar raised a concern about spill rate causing I/O tail spikes; added token-bucket rate limiter and CI stress tests; she approved after rerun. Author replies clarify decisions about opportunistic coalescing and cost model for selector. Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2024-12-02 after a successful re-run of CI and sign-off from reviewers. Notes: this PR focuses on reducing fragmentation-induced stalls and making eviction decisions more workload-aware; it intentionally does not change on-disk spill format or existing public configs beyond adding toggles and thresholds. For upgrade playbook see docs/ops/kv-tuning.md.

release_notes: Reduced KV-cache fragmentation and tail reclamation stalls by introducing a pager coalescer, selector/reclaim eviction refactor, and spill-rate control. Performance: up to 12% p95 latency improvement on mixed workloads and ~18% reduction in reclamation tail pauses. Config knobs added under kv.coalescer and kv.evictor. Non-breaking; default behavior unchanged.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature behind kv.coalescer.enabled=false to revert. Recommended canary: 5-10% traffic for 24-48h, monitor kv.region_fragmentation, kv.eviction_reclaim_latency, kv.spill_rate. If spill_rate grows unexpectedly, lower kv.evictor.spill_threshold or tighten kv.coalescer.rate_limit.
